neural responses to positive social feedback predict behavioral adjustments following social feedback in the context a real time social game.
the reward positivity (RewP), an event related potential (ERP) associated with reward processing, is associated with social behavior in a real time social feedback task.
neural responses to positive feedback from peers predict behavioral adjustments following that feedback.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain processes social information, particularly feedback about the self.
understanding the neural systems that drive human social behaviors.
the neural basis of social behavior and social decision-making in humans, with a particular emphasis on how people respond to feedback from other people.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current study provides evidence that neural responses to reward within 500 ms of receiving positive feedback from peers may guide subsequent social behavior, and may thus play a key role in the development of social relationships.
the reward positivity (RewP) is a neural marker of social reward processing that is associated with social behavior.

the RewP, an early neural response to reward, is associated with subsequent behavioral adjustments in a real time peer interaction task, such that participants who showed a larger RewP to positive social feedback were more likely to adjust their behavior accordingly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neural responses to social reward may be involved in the process of behavioral adjustment in response to social feedback, which is an important part of navigating the social landscape.
neural responses to social reward are associated with subsequent social behaviors in the context of real time interactions with others.
neural responses to social feedback are important predictors of social behaviors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neural responses to reward may play a role in guiding human social behaviors.
the brain is very sensitive to positive feedback, and this is important for how we behave in our daily lives.
